findings.issue_text: **Public group members page lost the ability to see the full member list, with no pagination UI added.**

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-33` now unconditionally caps every group's members at `limit=50`. But `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` and `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` were only patched to read `members` instead of `model` — no next/previous controls (unlike the admin template) were added. Before this PR, non-automatic groups returned an unbounded member list on this page. Now any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members silently shows only the first 50 with no way for a regular user to see the rest, and no indication data is truncated. This works against the PR's own goal of "proper handling of group memberships." Fix: add the same pagination affordance (or infinite scroll) used in `admin/templates/group.hbs` to the public members template/route.
**Off-by-one in `totalPages` causes a phantom empty last page whenever member count is an exact multiple of the page size.**
**`remove_member` can 500 on a stale/duplicate click, and neither add nor remove surfaces errors to the admin.**
**No test coverage for the core, breaking change to `GroupsController#members`.**

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62` ships with `// TODO: should clear the input` in the `addMembers` action — the username field isn't cleared after a successful add, inviting accidental duplicate submissions. Worth resolving before merge rather than leaving as a shipped TODO.

`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` — the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the actual route (`config/routes.rb`) maps `remove_member` to `DELETE`. The test still exercises the controller action correctly, but the verb is wrong and doesn't validate the real route/verb pairing.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound or negative-value guard (a negative limit would produce an invalid `LIMIT` in Postgres). This is a carry-over pattern from the old code, but since this PR is specifically about hardening membership handling/pagination, it's a good opportunity to clamp it (e.g., `[[limit, 1].max, 200].min`).

Renaming/removing `Group#createWithUsernames`/`#saveWithUsernames` and the `usernames` computed property is only verified against the one call site visible in this diff's scope; worth a quick repo-wide grep before merge to confirm no other caller (e.g. other admin views or specs not included in this change) still references the old API.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Public group members page lost the ability to see the full member list, with no pagination UI added.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit` (default 50) and `offset`, and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/members.json` with that pagination and sets `members` on the model. On the public group members page, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, while `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls or actions to change `offset`. Since `offset` is never advanced and there is no UI to request further pages, only the first page (up to 50 users) is visible and the full list is no longer accessible from that page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-33` now unconditionally caps every group's members at `limit=50`. But `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` and `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` were only patched to read `members` instead of `model` — no next/previous controls (unlike the admin template) were added. Before this PR, non-automatic groups returned an unbounded member list on this page. Now any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members silently shows only the first 50 with no way for a regular user to see the rest, and no indication data is truncated. This works against the PR's own goal of "proper handling of group memberships." Fix: add the same pagination affordance (or infinite scroll) used in `admin/templates/group.hbs` to the public members template/route.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination (`limit` defaults to 50, plus `offset`), whereas previously pagination/limit was only applied for `group.automatic?` and non-automatic groups returned the full member list. On the client, the public members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) was changed from setting the controller model to the returned members array to instead setting the model to the group and calling `model.findMembers()`, and the template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) was only adjusted to iterate `members`. However, unlike the admin UI, no next/previous actions or other pagination/infinite-scroll controls were added to the public members page, and nothing in this diff updates `offset` for subsequent loads. As a result, groups with >50 members will render only the first page with no obvious way to view the remainder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`remove_member` can 500 on a stale/duplicate click, and neither add nor remove surfaces errors to the admin.**
**No test coverage for the core, breaking change to `GroupsController#members`.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes a substantial behavior/response-shape change to `GroupsController#members` (from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to a custom JSON payload with `{members: ..., meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and new pagination semantics for all groups). In the shown test changes, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified; there is no added/updated spec covering `GroupsController#members` (no `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` changes, nor any assertions about the new `meta` fields or pagination behavior). So the finding that this core change lacks test coverage is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment in the `addMembers` action, and the controller does not explicitly reset `this.usernames` after calling `model.addMembers(...)`. However, this is not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone: (1) it’s a TODO/UX improvement rather than a correctness/security bug, and (2) the `user-selector` component may clear its bound value on selection/submission internally (not shown in the diff), so we can’t conclusively say the field “isn't cleared” in practice. The finding is therefore not a strict, diff-provable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound or negative-value guard (a negative limit would produce an invalid `LIMIT` in Postgres). This is a carry-over pattern from the old code, but since this PR is specifically about hardening membership handling/pagination, it's a good opportunity to clamp it (e.g., `[[limit, 1].max, 200].min`).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and immediately uses it in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping or validation. This is verifiable in the diff and allows a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit` (potentially causing heavy queries/memory use) and also to pass negative values (behavior becomes adapter/DB-dependent and can defeat pagination, even if it doesn’t always error). The finding’s core point—no upper bound/negative guard—is a real issue present in the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `Group#createWithUsernames`/`#saveWithUsernames` and the controller’s `usernames` computed property, and it updates the *visible* call sites in this diff (e.g., admin-group controller now calls `group.save()` / `group.create()`). However, the proposed finding is explicitly about *potential* other call sites elsewhere in the repo that might still reference the old API. That cannot be verified from the provided diff itself, so it’s speculative rather than a concrete defect introduced/shown here.
